summary: Sporadic 5xx affecting long-lived streaming sessions due to tenant priority inversion and model-fallback churn
description:
Issue summary:
We observed intermittent 5xx errors for a subset of long-lived streaming sessions for LexiHealth tenants during high concurrent usage windows. Errors surface as HTTP 502/503 from the API gateway with upstream runtime disconnects and repeated model-fallbacks.

Impact:
- Customer LexiHealth reporting increased error rates ~8-12% for streaming calls between 21:00-22:30 UTC on 2026-03-09 and again on 2026-03-10.
- Several production user flows (live transcription + context streaming) experienced dropped sessions and client reconnect storms.
- Customer is on a Dedicated plan and requires P1 response due to production outage for clinical demo traffic.

Environment:
- prod | us-east
- Dedicated GPU pool: dp-lexi-001 (NVIDIA H100)
- Ingress: api-gw-us-east-v2 behind ALB/HTTP2

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Initiate ~200 concurrent long-lived streaming sessions that maintain an open connection and periodically send small deltas (heartbeat + tokens).
2) After 15-25 minutes, a subset of sessions experiences probe failures from the runtime; API gateway returns 502 and triggers client reconnect logic.
3) Reconnections correlate with model-fallback events (runtime attempts to fallback to smaller model variant) and a transient increase in queue latency.

Observed behavior:
- API gateway logs show upstream RST/EOF and 502 responses.
- Serving runtime logs show frequent "fallback-to-variant" events and repeated cache invalidations for the same tenant.
- Ingress prioritizer metrics show a short window of priority inversion: low-latency short requests are being deprioritized in favor of inflight long-held streams, causing head-of-line blocking and preemption of worker threads.
- KV cache metrics show high eviction churn and increased cache-miss latency during the window.

Expected behavior:
- Long-lived streaming sessions should not block short synchronous requests; prioritizer should maintain fairness and avoid priority inversion. Model-fallbacks should be rate-limited to prevent cascade.

Logs/metrics attached (links):
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/lexihealth-5xx-burst
- API gateway trace: trace-id=9415b8c2-stream-burst
- Runtime logs excerpt: https://logs.redwood.ai/lexihealth/streams/2026-03-10/trace-9415b8c2

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-09 21:05 UTC: LexiHealth reports initial errors to CS.
- 2026-03-09 21:12 UTC: Support collects traces and opens SUP-612999.
- 2026-03-10 02:30 UTC: SRE observes correlated worker preemption events in dp-lexi-001 pool.
- 2026-03-10 21:00-22:30 UTC: Repeat elevated error window observed; automated mitigation (rate-limiting long streams) temporarily reduced errors.

Business risk:
- LexiHealth relies on deterministic streaming availability for clinical demos; repeated failures threaten ongoing trial and SLA compliance.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: tenant-level priority inversion combined with aggressive model-fallbacks under memory pressure. Evidence:
- Ingress prioritizer histogram shows burst where long streams consume accept-queue slots and worker threads; short requests queue behind them.
- Serving runtime shows increased model-fallback frequency (variant switch logs) and KV cache thrash causing prefetch timeouts.
- Correlation with Dedicated pool memory pressure spikes on the affected GPU nodes.
Actions taken so far:
- Temporarily applied per-tenant concurrent-stream cap (mitigation) which reduced error rate from ~10% -> ~1.8% during next window.
- Added emergency limiter to throttle model-fallback path to one fallback-per-tenant-per-10s.
- Captured heap and GPU memory profiles for dp-lexi-001 nodes and uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-debug/lexihealth/2026-03-10/heap-gpu-profiles.tar.gz
Next investigation steps:
1) Reproduce in staging with controlled long-stream load and artificial fallback churn.
2) Add precise instrumentation on prioritizer accept and worker preemption counters.
3) Validate KV cache eviction policy under streaming-dominant workload and consider per-tenant cache separation.
4) Review kernel selection logs to verify whether quantized kernel fallback contributed to slower token generation and backlog.
comments: 2026-03-10 21:18 - Priya Nair (Support): Collected traces from customer and escalated to SRE. Customer seeing ~11% error rate during demo hours. Asked for ETA on mitigation.

2026-03-10 22:05 - Jordan Lee (SRE): Applied temporary per-tenant stream cap and a conservative fallback throttle. Error rate dropped noticeably. Collecting longer retention traces. Assigned to Jordan for deeper root-cause analysis.

2026-03-11 09:12 - Carlos Mendes (Serving Runtime): Observed repeated \"variant-switch\" events correlated with GPU memory fragmentation. Opening runtime profiling PR to add more verbose variant-swap logs. Refer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1287
2026-03-11 14:44 - Priya Nair (Support): Customer acknowledged mitigation improved stability but requested permanent fix. Asked for timeline for config change or runtime fix.

2026-03-12 10:02 - Jordan Lee (SRE): Experimented in staging with per-tenant cache partitioning; initial results promising (reduced eviction churn). Scheduling canary for dp-lexi-001 with extended telemetry on 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC.
resolution: Mitigation deployed: temporary per-tenant streaming concurrency cap and throttle on model-fallback path. Canary of per-tenant cache partitioning scheduled to validate permanence. Follow-up engineering tasks created to change prioritizer fairness and make fallback rate-limits adaptive rather than reactive. Pending: full runtime patch to improve memory compaction during variant swaps. Close after successful canary and customer confirmation.
workaround: Applied per-tenant concurrent stream cap and limited fallback frequency (one fallback/10s). Customers advised to stagger large demo sessions and reduce simultaneous long-lived background streams until permanent fix is rolled out.
